=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/ai_labels.py
  Line or code reference: function `_label_sync_validation_error` at line 133
  Problem: Only validates description length (≤100 chars). Does not validate label name length against GitHub's 50-character maximum.
  Why it fails at runtime: Currently no contract label exceeds 50 chars (longest is `ai:orchestrator-validate-required` at 33 chars), so this does not trigger a runtime failure with the current contract. However, if a longer label name is added to the contract, the sync would attempt to create/update it, receive a 422 validation error from the GitHub API, and record it as a per-label error rather than catching it early.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/ai_labels.py
  Line or code reference: `_github_api_request` retry loop, lines 213-230; label-create POST call at lines 480-490
  Problem: The retry loop in `_github_api_request` replays POST (label-create) requests on transient 5xx/429 responses. If the first POST succeeded on the server (label was created) but the client received a 502/503 from an intermediate proxy, the retry POST would receive a 422 "already exists" and the error would be reported as a create failure even though the label was actually created.
  Why it fails at runtime: Requires a network partition between the GitHub API server and a proxy where the server accepts the create but the response is lost. The probability is extremely low — the client must receive a retryable status (429/5xx) after a successful server-side mutation. The label is not broken (it exists correctly), but the error reporting is misleading.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: .github/workflows/sync_ai_labels.yml
  Line or code reference: Summarize-results step, line 160: `f"- Repository: \`{Path.cwd().name}\`"`
  Problem: The step summary reports the repository name using `Path.cwd().name`, which drops the owner prefix (e.g., shows `myrepo` instead of `myorg/myrepo`). The CLI command already passes `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` (which includes the owner) to `--repo`, so the actual API calls target the correct full slug. But the human-readable summary is less informative than it could be, and operator diagnostics may be slightly harder.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not cause a runtime failure. The sync operation is unaffected — only the summary table display is less precise.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: "Add reusable workflow `.github/workflows/sync_ai_labels.yml` with `workflow_call` plus local `workflow_dispatch` support." Acceptance: "`sync_ai_labels.yml` can be dispatched locally and called as a reusable workflow."
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/sync_ai_labels.yml` — the contract-file resolution path (lines 59-62, or a preceding checkout step) must make the label contract file available when called as `workflow_call` from a consumer repository.
  Evidence of absence: The reusable workflow at lines 59-62 hardcodes `--contract-file .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` as a local path. The `actions/checkout@v5` step at line 38 checks out only the calling consumer repository (no `repository` parameter override and no secondary checkout of `coding-workflows@stable`). The `update_workflows.yml` workflow at line 77 runs `git sparse-checkout set workflow-templates scripts` — it syncs only `workflow-templates/` and `scripts/` to consumer repos; `.github/ai/` is intentionally excluded. The contract file does not exist in consumer repositories. When a consumer invokes this workflow via `workflow_call`, the Python CLI will raise `FileNotFoundError` on `--contract-file .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json`. The PR's own CI smoke test (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 466-483) passes only because it runs inside the `coding-workflows` repo where the contract file is present. The Copilot review comment at entry[5] identified this gap; the prior autofix editor marked the workflow as "already satisfied" and did not address it.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

- File: scripts/ai_labels.py
  Line or code reference: 133-138
  Problem: `_label_sync_validation_error` only validates description length (≤100 chars) but does NOT validate label name length. GitHub enforces a 50-character maximum on label names.
  Why it fails at runtime: Labels with names >50 characters will reach the GitHub API and receive 422 validation errors, causing sync failures. The dry-run smoke test passes but real sync operations will fail with partial errors.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/sync_ai_labels.yml
  Line or code reference: 59-60
  Problem: The reusable workflow hardcodes `--contract-file .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` as a local path. Consumer repos do not have this file because `update_workflows.yml` (line 77) only syncs `workflow-templates/` and `scripts/` to consumers, not `.github/ai/`.
  Why it fails at runtime: When the workflow is invoked as `workflow_call` from a consumer repo (via the wrapper), the script will fail with FileNotFoundError because the contract file doesn't exist in the consumer's checkout. This breaks the core acceptance criterion: "sync_ai_labels.yml can be dispatched locally and called as a reusable workflow."
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- File: .github/workflows/sync_ai_labels.yml
  Line or code reference: 158
  Problem: The step summary uses `Path.cwd().name` which only shows the checkout repo name (e.g., "coding-workflows") without the owner, rather than using `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}` which contains the full `owner/repo` of the target repository being synced.
  Why it fails at runtime: When invoked as a reusable workflow from a consumer wrapper, the summary displays the wrong repository name. Operators cannot reliably identify which repo was actually synced.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
